aspects.says: a.andThen(b) runs a, then b, on the same value, and if a throws, b does not run and the exception reaches the caller; so the step that can refuse goes first and the irreversible one last.
basis: section:andThen Runs the Steps in Order, and Stops at the First One That Throws

aspects.says: andThen is a sequence, not a transaction: a step that ran stays done when a later step throws, and that exception reaches the caller.
basis: section:andThen Runs the Steps in Order, and Stops at the First One That Throws

aspects.says: andThen(null) throws NullPointerException when the chain is built, not when it runs, so an optional step needs an explicit choice.
basis: section:A Null Step Fails When the Chain Is Built, Not When It Runs

aspects.says: On a parallel stream forEach calls the Consumer from several threads at once and in no order, so a target that is not thread-safe loses elements; collect, then hand the result over from one thread, or use forEachOrdered.
basis: section:On a Parallel Stream, forEach Calls the Consumer from Several Threads, in No Order

aspects.says: A stream calls peek's Consumer only for the elements its terminal operation pulls: all, one for findFirst, none for count() on a sized source or with no terminal operation, so a required side effect goes in a terminal forEach or a loop.
basis: section:A Stream Calls Your Consumer Only for the Elements It Needs, and peek May Not Run at All

aspects.says: A lambda or method reference whose expression returns a value, such as seen::add, still compiles as a Consumer and the value is dropped, so a step whose result the caller needs is not a Consumer.
basis: section:A Consumer Is Called for Its Side Effect, and Whatever the Lambda Returns Is Dropped

aspects.says: map and sorted keep the stream's size, so count() after them skips a peek as well; a filter hides the size and the pipeline runs.
basis: section:A Stream Calls Your Consumer Only for the Elements It Needs, and peek May Not Run at All

aspects.says: A thread-safe target, or a lock around the Consumer, keeps every element of a parallel forEach but not the source order.
basis: section:On a Parallel Stream, forEach Calls the Consumer from Several Threads, in No Order

aspects.says: Map.forEach takes a BiConsumer of key and value, Optional.ifPresentOrElse a Consumer and a Runnable, IntStream.forEach an IntConsumer and IntStream.collect an ObjIntConsumer accumulator.
basis: section:A Consumer Is Called for Its Side Effect, and Whatever the Lambda Returns Is Dropped
aspects.reason: which interface a JDK method takes is checked by the compiler, so a practice has no wrong solution that compiles; the Reference table holds the lookup
